newsitem.title: UK: UK's Camelot comms director Rigg to quit.
newsitem.headline: UK's Camelot comms director Rigg to quit.

text.p: Britain's national lottery operator Camelot Group Plc said on Monday that its director of communications, David Rigg, would leave the company on October 3, 1997.
Rigg was one of the Camelot directors caught up in a row with UK's Labour government over huge rises in annual salaries at the lottery operator.
Camelot is a consortium of Racal Electronics Plc, De La Rue Plc, GTECH, Cadbury Schweppes Plc and Fujitsu Ltd's ICL.
Rigg considered resigning in June, after a political storm broke when details of Camelot's executive pay rise was leaked to the press.
Bonuses inflated Camelot's executive wage bill by 40 percent at a time when money raised for good causes actually fell.

The stand-off between Camelot's executives and British Culture Secretary Chris Smith ended with a compromise agreement, which saw Camelot's main executives agreeing to contribute some of forthcoming long-term bonuses to a charity fund.
Since the lottery was launched in 1994, Camelot has raised over 3.0 billion stg for good causes including sports, arts and various charitable causes.
